chunks: And from him (Al-Hassan ibn Ma'mar) from Ibn Abi Umayr and Safwan from Abd al-Rahman, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) asked me: 'Do Ibn Abi Layl and Ibn Shubrumah differ?' I said to him: 'It reached me that a freed slave of Isa ibn Musa died, leaving a large debt upon him, and he left boys whose debt encompassed their value, and he freed them at the time of death.' So he asked them about that. Ibn Shubrumah said: 'I see that they should be assessed for their value, and that amount should be paid to the creditors, for he had freed them at the time of his death.' And Ibn Abi Layl said: 'I see that they should be sold and their price paid to the creditors, for it is not for him to free them at the time of his death while he has a debt that encompasses them.' And this is the people of Al-Hijaz today: a man frees his slave while he has a large debt, so they do not validate his manumission if there is a large debt upon him.

Then Ibn Shubrumah raised his hand to the sky and said: 'Glory be to Allah, O Ibn Abi Layl, when did you say this opinion? By Allah, if you said it, it was only to seek opposition to me.' He said to me: 'From whose opinion did it originate?' I said: 'It reached me that he followed the opinion of Ibn Abi Layl, and he had a preference for that, so he sold them and paid off his debt.'

He said: 'With which of them is the people from your side?' I said: 'With Ibn Shubrumah.' And Ibn Abi Layl had returned to the opinion of Ibn Shubrumah after that. He said: 'By Allah, indeed the truth is in what Ibn Abi Layl said, even though he had returned from it.'

I said: 'This is broken/rejected in their analogy (qiyas).' He said: 'Come, let me reason with you.' I said: 'I will reason with you.' He said: 'You will say with the strongest thing that enters into the analogy.' I said to him: 'A man left a slave, leaving no wealth other than him, and the value of the slave is six hundred, and his debt is five hundred, so he freed him at the time of death. What is done in his case?' He said: 'He is sold, and the creditors take five hundred, and the heirs take one hundred.'

I said: 'Is it not that there remained from the value of the slave one hundred dirhams for his debt?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Is it not that the man has one-third of his wealth which he does with what he wishes?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'Did he not bequeath to the slave one-third of that one hundred when he freed him?' He said: 'Indeed, the slave has no bequest; his wealth is for his masters.'

I said: 'And if the value of the slave is six hundred dirhams and his debt is four hundred dirhams?' He said: 'So the slave is sold, the creditors take four hundred, and the heirs take two hundred, and the slave has nothing.'

I said: 'And if the value of the slave is six hundred dirhams and his debt is three hundred dirhams?' He laughed and said: 'From here your companions were misled; they made the things one thing and did not know the Sunnah. When the wealth of the creditors and the wealth of the heirs are equal, or if the wealth of the heirs is more than the wealth of the creditors, the man is not suspected regarding his bequest, and the bequest is validated as it is. Now this slave is held: half of him is for the creditors, one-third is for the heirs, and one-sixth is for him.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report is consistent with the first hadith narrated by Zurarah, which states that manumission is only valid if the price is double the debt. The two reports are not contradictory to the first report narrated by Al-Halabi, which states that if the price does not cover the debt, the remainder is assessed, because it is not impossible that the meaning of the first report is that if the price does not cover the debt, but is less than it by half the debt, then the manumission is valid. As for his saying 'If the slave's price covers the debt, the manumission is void,' all the hadiths agree on that. The two later reports add the detail we mentioned, and this detail does not contradict the report we preceded from Hisham ibn Salim, that whoever bought a girl for a year and freed her and did not possess at the time what covers her price, the manumission is not valid, because that report is restricted to when the debt is from the price of the girl; if he did not possess that, the manumission is not valid. The other hadiths are understood to be when the debt is not from the price of the owned person, and the owned person is freed; then in that case, the doubling of the price is observed as we preceded.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a deceased owner's manumission of a slave if the slave's value is less than the owner's debt?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the conditions for valid manumission (itq) when debt is present, establishing that if the slave's value is double the debt, the bequest of freedom is upheld; otherwise, the slave is sold to pay creditors. The Imam demonstrates the superiority of the Ahl al-Bayt's reasoning over the jurists of Hijaz by showing how their rigid application of qiyas (analogical reasoning) fails to account for proportional distribution when the slave's value is insufficient to cover the full debt, whereas the Sunnah allows for a fair split between creditors and heirs.
